references.text: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is first mentioned as one of the spies sent to explore the land of Canaan.
Joshua, son of Nun, is mentioned as the representative from the tribe of Ephraim among the twelve spies.
Caleb tried to calm the people and encouraged them to enter the land, showing his faith and courage.
Joshua and Caleb were the only spies allowed to enter the Promised Land because of their faithfulness.
Joshua and Caleb survived as the only spies because they trusted in the Lord.
Reuben tore his clothes as an expression of grief, the same action performed by Joshua and Caleb.
Jacob tore his clothes in grief over Joseph, a parallel to tearing one's garments as a sign of deep sorrow.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face before the ark of the Lord after the defeat at Ai, the same expression of grief.
David and his men tore their clothes when they heard about the deaths of Saul and Jonathan, the same mourning ritual.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, was promised that he would see the land because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
